_note: Real items from UK Parliament APIs, 23-27 Nov 2026, in the APIs' own field layout. Question, answer and statement text is paraphrased (shortened) because the originals couldn't be downloaded in the build environment. Items whose heading starts 'TEST ONLY' are synthetic and exist only to test filtering; they must never appear in a briefing.

writtenquestions.heading: Transport: Wales
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks what assessment the Government has made of how transport connectivity within Wales affects its economic growth.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says transport links are vital to Wales's growth by connecting people to jobs, education and services, and refers to a commitment to transforming Welsh rail.

writtenquestions.heading: Social Security Benefits: Take-up
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks for an assessment of how effective the Scottish Government's Benefit Take-Up Strategy 2026-2031, and its predecessors, have been in raising take-up of devolved social security benefits.
writtenquestions.answerText: Points to GOV.UK for information on reserved DWP benefits and says help to claim is available from the Department and trusted third parties.

writtenquestions.heading: Glyphosate
writtenquestions.answeringBodyName: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks whether funding should be provided to councils in England and Wales that want to stop using glyphosate.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says glyphosate is strictly regulated in Great Britain and approved only if it will not harm human or animal health or pose unacceptable environmental risks.

writtenquestions.heading: Glyphosate
writtenquestions.answeringBodyName: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks what assessment has been made of how glyphosate concentrations in rainwater might affect crop yields in England and Wales.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says glyphosate is strictly regulated in Great Britain and approved only if it poses no unacceptable risks.

writtenquestions.heading: Stalking Protection Orders: Enforcement
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks what arrangements exist so Stalking Protection Orders can be pursued and enforced when an offender has no fixed address or a transient lifestyle.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says Stalking Protection Orders can be sought and enforced regardless of a fixed address, and points to the statutory police guidance.

writtenquestions.heading: Domestic Abuse: Mediation
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks what steps are being taken to stop sharia councils pressuring women and girls into mediation with perpetrators of domestic abuse.
writtenquestions.answerText: States that no victim should be pressured to stay in an abusive relationship and that religious freedom cannot shield criminal conduct.

writtenquestions.heading: Economic Growth and Industry: Wales
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks about discussions with the Welsh Government on ensuring Wales benefits from the Government's industrial strategy and growth mission.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says driving growth in every postcode is a priority and that the Prime Minister offered at the National Economic Council on 30 October 2026 to work with the Welsh Government.

writtenquestions.heading: Public Sector: Wales
writtenquestions.questionText: Asks for an assessment of trends in public service outcomes in devolved areas of Wales and what they mean for the devolution settlement.
writtenquestions.answerText: Says the Government is providing the Welsh Government an extra £450 million for devolved public services on top of the settlement, rising in real terms over the Spending Review period.
